advances: Determines the order of the global minimum over the entire ternary-box exponential family and rules out a lower bound by fourth powers of parity-class masses at finite local minima.
author: research-agent
external_sources:
Ilya Tyurin, "New Estimates of the Convergence Rate in the Lyapunov Theorem," arXiv:0912.0726v1, equation (1):
https://arxiv.org/html/0912.0726v1

The theorem used is the existence of an absolute \(C_{\rm BE}\) such that independent centered real variables \(X_i\), with total variance \(\sigma^2>0\) and finite third absolute moments, satisfy
\[
\sup_t\left|
\mathbb P\left(\sum_iX_i/\sigma\le t\right)-\Phi(t)
\right|
\le C_{\rm BE}\sigma^{-3}\sum_i\mathbb E|X_i|^3.
\]
Here \(X_i=\lambda_iU_i\); independence, centering, finite moments, and the required Lyapunov-ratio bound were checked above.
proof:
Write
\[
Z_j=1+2\cosh\theta_j,\quad A_j=2\cosh4\theta_j,
\quad
T_I=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\{-1,0,1\}^{I}}
e^{-|\sum_{j\in I}\theta_ju_j|}.
\]
After translating the support in accepted fact 089a4139d9314589 and reflecting coordinates with positive tilt, its exact actual-depth formula gives
\[
\tau_p(\mathbf z)=p_{\mathbf z}(T_{I(\mathbf z)}+1)/2,
\qquad I(\mathbf z)=\{j:z_j=0\}.
\]
Zero tilt coordinates follow by continuity, since each depth is a minimum of finitely many linear mass functions. Therefore
\[
F_{D_N}(\bm{\theta})
=\frac1{8\prod_jZ_j^4}
\sum_{I\subseteq[N]}(T_I+1)^3\prod_{j\notin I}A_j. \tag{1}
\]

For finite attainment, proceed inductively. A boundary law in the compact closure of the ternary product family fixes at least one coordinate at an endpoint and is a finite ternary tilt in the remaining coordinates. Its moment equals the moment on that lower-dimensional face.

Given a finite minimizing law in dimension \(N-1\), with depths \(t_{\mathbf z}\), add a coordinate with weights \(B,1,B^{-1}\). The outer layers can be isolated. A cap at a middle-layer point can exclude the heavy layer, realize the chosen middle-layer cap, and include the light layer. Thus
\[
F_{D_N}\le
\frac{(B^4+B^{-4})v_{N-1}
+\mathbb E_p(t_{\mathbf Z}+B^{-1})^3}
{(B+1+B^{-1})^4}
=v_{N-1}(1-4/B+O(B^{-2}))+O(B^{-4}).
\]
For large \(B\), this is below \(v_{N-1}\). Every boundary value is at least \(v_{N-1}\), using the preceding strict inequalities inductively. Compactness and continuity therefore give finite attainment and \(v_N<v_{N-1}\).

We next prove a small-ball estimate. For every fixed \(B>0\), there is \(b_B>0\) such that
\[
\sum_{\mathbf u\in\{-1,0,1\}^k}
e^{-|\sum_i\lambda_i u_i|}
\ge b_B3^k/\sqrt{k+1}
\quad\text{whenever }|\lambda_i|\le B. \tag{2}
\]
Let \(U_i\) be independent uniform ternary variables and \(S=\sum_i\lambda_iU_i\). Then
\[
\sigma^2=\tfrac23\sum_i\lambda_i^2,\qquad
\sum_i\mathbb E|\lambda_iU_i|^3\le B\sigma^2.
\]
The nonidentically distributed Berry-Esseen theorem gives error at most \(C_{\rm BE}B/\sigma\) when \(\sigma>0\).

Choose a sufficiently large absolute \(L\). If \(\sigma\le LB\), Chebyshev gives \(\mathbb P(|S|\le2LB)\ge3/4\). Otherwise, the standard normal probability of this interval is at least \(cLB/\sigma\); subtracting the two Berry-Esseen errors and choosing \(L\) sufficiently large gives probability at least \(c'B/\sigma\ge c''/\sqrt{k}\). Multiplication by \(e^{-2LB}\) proves (2). The case \(\sigma=0\) is immediate.

Define
\[
a(t)=\frac{2\cosh4t+27}{(1+2\cosh t)^4},
\qquad
b(t)=\frac{2\cosh4t}{(1+2\cosh t)^4}.
\]
With \(x=2\cosh t\), the derivative of \(a\) with respect to \(x\) is
\[
\frac{4(x^3+2x^2-2x-29)}{(x+1)^5}.
\]
Hence \(a\) has its unique minimum in \(|t|\) at \(\theta_*\), with value \(a_*\). Since \(b(t)\to1\), fix \(B>\theta_*\) and \(b_0>a_*\) such that \(b(t)\ge b_0\) for \(|t|>B\).

For an arbitrary tilt, let \(S=\{j:|\theta_j|\le B\}\). In (1), retain only \(I\subseteq S\) and apply (2). Expanding the remaining product gives
\[
F_{D_N}(\bm{\theta})
\ge\frac{b_B^3}{8(N+1)^{3/2}}
\prod_{j\in S}a(\theta_j)\prod_{j\notin S}b(\theta_j)
\ge C_1(N+1)^{-3/2}a_*^N. \tag{3}
\]

For the upper bound, use only the trial parameter \((\theta_*,\ldots,\theta_*)\). Fourier inversion gives
\[
\sup_r\mathbb P(U_1+\cdots+U_k=r)
\le\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}
\left|\frac{1+2\cos t}{3}\right|^kdt
\le C/\sqrt{k+1}.
\]
The final estimate follows from a quadratic bound near zero and a strict bound below one on its complement. Since \(\sum_{r\in\mathbb Z}e^{-\theta_*|r|}<\infty\),
\[
T_I+1\le C'3^{|I|}/\sqrt{|I|+1}.
\]
Substituting into (1), with \(A_*=2\cosh4\theta_*\), yields
\[
F_{D_N}(\theta_*,\ldots,\theta_*)
\le Ca_*^N\mathbb E(K+1)^{-3/2},
\]
where \(K\sim\operatorname{Bin}(N,27/(A_*+27))\). Splitting at half the mean and using the exponential lower-tail bound proves the required upper estimate.

At a global minimizer, compare (3) with that upper estimate. The common polynomial factor cancels, leaving
\[
\sum_{j\in S}\log\frac{a(\theta_j)}{a_*}
+|S^c|\log\frac{b_0}{a_*}\le C.
\]
Every summand is nonnegative. The second term bounds \(|S^c|\), and compactness plus uniqueness of the minimum of \(a\) proves the coordinate-clustering assertion.

The two parity masses in coordinate \(j\) are \(1/Z_j\) and \(2\cosh\theta_j/Z_j\). Thus
\[
\sum_{\mathbf c}\alpha_{\mathbf c}^4
=\prod_j
\frac{(2\cosh\theta_j)^4+1}{(1+2\cosh\theta_j)^4}.
\]
Each factor lies in \([17/81,1]\). Clustering therefore makes its \(N\)-th root converge to \(c_*\), whereas the moment bounds give \(v_N^{1/N}\to a_*\).

The defining cubic is negative at \(\sqrt7\), so \(x_*>\sqrt7\). Hence
\[
c_*-a_*=\frac{4(x_*^2-7)}{(x_*+1)^4}>0,
\qquad
a_*>\frac{50}{256}>\frac18.
\]
These inequalities prove the final two limits.
statement:
For \(D_N=\{-1,0,1\}^N\), let
\[
p_{\bm{\theta}}(\mathbf z)
=\frac{e^{\bm{\theta}\cdot\mathbf z}}{Z_{D_N}(\bm{\theta})},
\quad
\tau_p(\mathbf z)=\min_{H\ni\mathbf z}p(H),
\quad
F_{D_N}(\bm{\theta})=\sum_{\mathbf z}p_{\bm{\theta}}(\mathbf z)
\tau_{p_{\bm{\theta}}}(\mathbf z)^3,
\]
where all halfspaces are closed. Put \(v_N=\inf_{\bm{\theta}}F_{D_N}(\bm{\theta})\) and \(v_0=1\).

Let \(x_*\in(2,3)\) be the unique root of
\[
x^3+2x^2-2x-29=0,
\]
and define
\[
\theta_*=\operatorname{arcosh}(x_*/2),\quad
a_*=\frac{x_*^4-4x_*^2+29}{(x_*+1)^4},\quad
c_*=\frac{x_*^4+1}{(x_*+1)^4}.
\]
There are absolute \(C_1,C_2>0\) such that
\[
C_1(N+1)^{-3/2}a_*^N
\le v_N\le C_2(N+1)^{-3/2}a_*^N.
\]
Furthermore, \(v_N<v_{N-1}\), every global minimizer is finite, and for each \(\delta>0\) there is \(C_\delta<\infty\), independent of \(N\), such that every global minimizer satisfies
\[
\#\{j:\ ||\theta_j|-\theta_*|\ge\delta\}\le C_\delta.
\]

For any sequence of global-minimizer laws \(p_N\), let
\(\alpha_{\mathbf c}=p_N(D_N\cap(\mathbf c+2\mathbb Z^N))\). Then
\[
\left(\frac{M_3(p_N)}{\sum_{\mathbf c}\alpha_{\mathbf c}^4}\right)^{1/N}
\to\frac{a_*}{c_*}<1,
\qquad
8^NM_3(p_N)\to\infty.
\]
